sources.title: Fangs of Du Couteau: The Complete Cassiopeia Guide

passive.name: Serpentine Grace
passive.text: All Move Speed bonuses are more effective on Cassiopeia.

spells.name: Noxious Blast
spells.text: Cassiopeia blasts an area with Poison after a brief delay, granting her increased Move Speed if she hits an enemy champion.

spells.name: Miasma
spells.text: Cassiopeia releases several clouds of poison, slowing, grounding, and lightly damaging enemies that pass through them. Grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities.

spells.name: Twin Fang
spells.text: Cassiopeia lets loose an attack that deals increased damage to Poisoned targets and heals her for a percentage of the damage dealt. If the target dies from this attack, Cassiopeia regains Mana.

spells.name: Petrifying Gaze
spells.text: Cassiopeia releases a swirl of magical energy from her eyes, stunning any enemies in front of her that are facing her and slowing any others with their back turned.

damage.value: Cassiopeia deals sustained poison-based mage damage rather than relying on burst.

archetype.value: Cassiopeia is a DPS mage who controls space and punishes dives.

axis.value: Cassiopeia favors long trades because her sustained damage excels in extended fights.

winCondition.value: Cassiopeia wins by positioning safely and dealing sustained damage through teamfights.

spikes.why: Cassiopeia gains a larger mana pool, AP scaling, and a defensive shield.
Cassiopeia gains health-based burn that strengthens her sustained damage.
Cassiopeia can slow with her poison to kite more effectively.

bait.why: Cassiopeia cannot ground enemies with Miasma again until its long cooldown ends.

mistakes.value: Cassiopeia players who position poorly leave her vulnerable despite her late-game damage.
Cassiopeia loses Twin Fang’s increased damage and healing when she uses it on a target that is not poisoned.
